criteria.name: The governance of the institution is clearly defined in the organizational structure.
The policy-making body demonstrates strong leadership and supports the institution's programs and operations.
Conflict in administrative jurisdictions and official relationships are minimal.
Clear institutional policies and codes of conduct govern ethical practices across all operations.
The organization follows institutional processes with respect to governance because leadership was selected based on transparent procedures.
Stakeholders express high trust and satisfaction in transparent management.
Management is guided by a well-defined institutional vision and mission consonance with regional, national, and global trends.
The institution implements the Strategic Plan and periodically evaluates it through Agency Performance Reviews.
Key developmental milestones in the Strategic Plan are achieved on schedule.
There is a sound system of management, budget allocation, and financial control.
The university executes rigid monitoring of income-generating projects and fund utilization.
Fund utilization is effective and transparent with minimal audit observations.
Academic programs have clearly defined objectives and learning outcomes aligned with the institution's VMGO.
Periodic review and evaluation of academic programs are conducted incorporating labor market and stakeholder demands.
Graduates demonstrate desired program competencies and achieve high employability.
Curricula reflect outcomes-based education (OBE) principles and conform to CHED standards.
Innovative instructional methodologies, flexible learning, and blended coursework are deployed.
A merit selection plan and transparent qualification standards govern the recruitment and promotion of faculty and staff.
Hiring and promotion processes strictly observe publication requirements, objective scoring, and odd-numbered voting boards.
The institution maintains a highly qualified corps of full-time faculty holding vertically articulated graduate degrees.
A comprehensive Faculty and Staff Development Program (FSDP) provides scholarships, grants, and study leaves.
Faculty members participate in local, national, and international training, research conferences, and post-graduate studies.
The institutional Research, Development, and Extension (RDE) Agenda is approved and aligned with national and regional priorities.
Research grants, workload deloading, and incentive mechanisms support faculty research initiatives.
Faculty publish in Scopus/WoS indexed journals, secure external grants, and register intellectual properties.
The institutional extension agenda and operational manual guide community engagement and technology transfer.
Extension programs are implemented in partnership with LGUs, civil society, and adopted communities.
Community impact assessments demonstrate sustained socioeconomic improvement in partner localities.
A comprehensive Student Affairs and Services (SAS) program provides holistic student development.
Career placement, counseling, scholarships, and mental health services are available across all campuses.
Comprehensive graduate tracer studies demonstrate positive alumni career trajectories and employer satisfaction.

parameters.name: Library Administration, Holdings, and Digital Resources

criteria.name: The university library is administered by licensed professional librarians with sufficient holdings and e-resources.
Online public access catalogs (OPAC) and remote electronic databases are accessible to all faculty and students.
High utilization rates of library and research facilities are recorded across all colleges.

parameters.name: Campus Master Plan and Physical Facilities

criteria.name: The Land Use Development and Infrastructure Plan (LUDIP) guides physical campus modernization and development.
Academic buildings, laboratories, and safety infrastructure meet national statutory standards and accessibility law (BP 344).
Learning spaces provide an environment conducive to instruction, research, and campus life.

parameters.name: Internal Quality Assurance Office and Systems

criteria.name: A dedicated, fully equipped Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) Office spearheads university-wide quality assurance.
A Quality Management System (QMS) aligned with ISO 9001:2015 is implemented with periodic internal quality audits.
Institutional and program accreditation levels are systematically monitored, maintained, and elevated.
